claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

claimant_dispute_unresolved.description: Whether two responsible claimants cannot agree who should claim Child Benefit.

conversation.text:
I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit. To assess your eligibility, I need to ask you a few questions.

First, do you have any children you're responsible for?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I do. I have a 3-year-old son named Alex who lives with me at home.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. So you have a 3-year-old son named Alex who lives with you.

Now, do you currently live in the UK?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I live in the UK.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great, thank you. A few more questions to complete the assessment:

Do you have settled status, pre-settled status under the EU Settlement Scheme, or are you a British citizen with the right to reside in the UK?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I do have the right to reside in the UK.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Excellent. Just to confirm - is anyone else currently claiming Child Benefit for Alex, such as another parent or guardian?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Well, actually, there is a bit of a situation there. Alex's other parent and I are both responsible for him, but we can't agree on who should claim the Child Benefit.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for clarifying that situation. I understand you and Alex's other parent both feel responsible for him but can't agree on who should claim.

Just to understand the living arrangements better - does Alex live with you full-time, or does he split his time between you and his other parent?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: He lives with me full-time at home.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
## Assessment Complete

**Good news! You are ELIGIBLE to claim Child Benefit for Alex.**

Here's why:

✓ Alex is 3 years old (under 16)  
✓ You live in the UK and have the right to reside  
✓ Alex lives with you full-time, which means you're responsible for him  

**Important note about the disagreement:** While only one person can receive Child Benefit for the same child, the fact that you and Alex's other parent can't agree on who should claim doesn't make you ineligible. You have every right to apply. If both of you make claims, HMRC will decide who will receive the benefit. Since Alex lives with you full-time, you have a strong case.

You can proceed with making a claim for Child Benefit. However, please be aware:
- If either you or your partner has an individual income over £60,000, you may have to pay the High Income Child Benefit tax charge
- You should consider discussing this with Alex's other parent to avoid competing claims, but you're not required to reach an agreement before applying

Would you like any additional information about how to make a claim or anything else?

reasonings: Alex is a 3-year-old child who is under 16 years old. The claimant lives in the UK and has the right to reside in the UK. Alex lives with the claimant full-time, which means the claimant is responsible for Alex under the rules (as they live together). According to the rules, only one person can get Child Benefit for a child. Even though both parents cannot agree on who should claim, the claimant qualifies for Child Benefit as they meet all the eligibility criteria: (1) responsible for a child under 16, (2) lives in the UK, (3) has right to reside, and (4) the child lives with them. The rules state that if two people cannot agree on who should claim, HMRC will decide who gets it, but this does not make the claimant ineligible - they are eligible to claim. The disagreement is an administrative matter that HMRC will resolve if both parties make claims.
